question.text: If a flagstaff of 6 metres high placed on the top of a tower throws a shadow of \(2 \sqrt{3}\) metres along the ground, then the angle (in degrees) that the sun makes with the ground is

solution.text:
Accordingly, \(\tan \theta=\frac{h}{x}=\frac{h+6}{x+2 \sqrt{3}}=\frac{6}{2 \sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \theta=60^{\circ}\)
